newsitem.title: DUBAI: Strong demand for Dubai gold on weak price.
newsitem.headline: Strong demand for Dubai gold on weak price.

text.p: Bullion prices at 3-1/4 year lows have prompted strong wholesale and retail gold demand in the Gulf re-export centre of Dubai, local traders said on Sunday.

Widespread speculation on more central bank selling has sent gold below $350 an ounce, a psychological level for Gulf and Indian subcontinent buyers, many of whom are also set to celebrate the end of the Moslem holy fasting month of Ramadan.
The Eid al-Fitr holiday, which marks Ramadan's end and is expected around February 10, is usually marked with the exchange of gifts, often in jewellery or bullion.

"Demand is extremely good at the moment...Demand has gone up because of the low price so no one wants to miss the train. (Ramadan) demand is stronger than last year when prices were higher," one Dubai-based trader said.
Import demand into Dubai from its main Swiss and British suppliers also remained upbeat, wholesalers said. December imports into Dubai totalled a robust 31.96 tonnes.
Bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $344.60-$345.10 an ounce, its lowest level since September 1993 and well below the year-on-year comparison of $415.10.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24-carat gold -- was quoted by traders at 4,767 UAE dirhams ($1,298) on Sunday, down from 4,880 dirhams ($1,329) on January 26.
TT bars were quoted at 5,055 dirhams at the start of 1997 but have tracked sliding world prices since the fourth quarter.

Demand into India was also being fanned by the Indian government's decision in December to allow Non-Resident Indians (NRI) to import 10 kg of gold every six months at a customs duty of 220 rupees ($6.13) per 10 grams (0.35 oz), traders said.
NRIs were previously allowed to import five kg.
"Carriers (to India) are approaching us each day...the new import regulations are feeding through," a trader said, referring to expatriate non-residents who carry gold on their return home.
Stable Indian rupee-U.S. dollar rates were also encouraging the Dubai-India gold route, traders said.
